title: NOUNS AFTER HOURS — Ten Four-Page Mini-Issues

issues.title: Clocking Out
issues.logline: Desk Buddy finishes every reopening task except finding a reason to stay.

cover.title: Clocking Out
cover.logline: Desk Buddy finishes every reopening task except finding a reason to stay.
cover.tagline: THE CHECKLIST ENDS. THE NIGHT BEGINS.
cover.scene: A small desktop window opens onto a giant midnight cinema. Desk Buddy holds a clipboard; Relay carries one mismatched chair. A blank marquee towers above them.

note.title: The Fourth Box
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: Midnight on a desktop. Three checklist boxes are filled. A tiny door appears beside the final checkmark.
panels.caption: Night one. Everything was done.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: Then why am I still here?

panels.scene: Desk Buddy and Relay stand beneath a dark cinema marquee. Relay holds a folded chair as if it were a parcel.
panels.caption: The exit led to The Between.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: Apparently the way out has seating.

panels.scene: Inside the lobby, a brass plate reads OPEN FOR WHAT? Desk Buddy opens a clipboard with three fresh empty boxes.
panels.caption: A very manageable question.

panels.scene: Desk Buddy switches on a lamp. Relay unfolds two chairs. Each chair has a tiny label reading FRONT, but they face opposite walls.
panels.caption: The plan had excellent labels.

panels.scene: A perfectly square sign reading READY hangs in the lobby. Both characters admire the three completed boxes. The auditorium is otherwise empty.
panels.caption: Three tasks. Three checks.

panels.scene: Close on Desk Buddy’s clipboard. Below the completed list sits a large, accidental blank space.
panels.caption: The blank part was bigger.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: I did not put that on the list.

panels.scene: Relay places both chairs beside one another, facing the screen. Desk Buddy stays standing with the clipboard held like a shield.
panels.caption: Relay proposed a fourth step.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: Sit with me for a minute.

panels.scene: Relay sets an empty paper cup in front of the projector. Its shadow becomes a huge, slightly ridiculous tower on the screen.
panels.caption: A building permit was unnecessary.

panels.scene: Desk Buddy tilts the clipboard across the projector beam. Its shadow becomes a roof above the cup tower.
panels.caption: The plan found a second use.

panels.scene: Both sit. The cup tower and clipboard roof form a tiny shadow cinema inside the real cinema. The empty fourth checkbox remains visible.
panels.caption: Nothing got completed for a while.

panels.scene: Pale dawn enters the lobby. Desk Buddy writes COME BACK beneath the three completed tasks and leaves its box empty. Relay folds one chair.
panels.caption: Dawn asked them to return.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: I want this one to stay open.

panels.scene: On the box-office counter rests a collectible note marked 1 BEGINNING. Desk Buddy turns it over to reveal the single printed word A.
panels.caption: The first souvenir was a beginning.

backPage.title: Meet Desk Buddy
backPage.shortBio: Excellent at getting things done. Learning to stay after the work is over.
fieldGuide: Favorite tool: three small boxes.
Secret fear: being invited only because something needs doing.
New skill: leaving a good thing unfinished.
backPage.bonusObject: A four-box pocket card: LIGHTS / CHAIRS / SIGN / COME BACK. Leave the last box open.
backPage.readerPrompt: Name one thing you would enjoy doing without measuring the result.
backPage.nextIssue: #02 The Long Way In — Scout investigates three routes to the same door.

issues.title: The Long Way In
issues.genre: A miniature heist with no stolen treasure
issues.logline: Scout plans the perfect way into the cinema and forgets that a door can simply open.

cover.title: The Long Way In
cover.logline: Scout plans the perfect way into the cinema and forgets that a door can simply open.
cover.tagline: THE BIGGEST SCORE IS PICKING A DOOR.
cover.scene: Scout studies a dramatic route map under a single lamp. Keeper holds an ordinary front-door key. Three dotted routes circle the same tiny cinema.

note.title: A Route Worth Taking
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: On a record-stall crate, Scout spreads a map of The Between. Three routes are labeled DRAMATIC, DAMP and CONVENIENT.
panels.caption: Night two. A proper operation.

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: We need the best way in.

panels.scene: Scout attaches colored thread to three pins. Keeper points to the plain door one step behind them.
panels.caption: Convenient lacked atmosphere.

panels.scene: The dramatic route leads to an alley ladder. A sign on the ladder reads LADDER DISPLAY. PLEASE USE DOOR.
panels.caption: Route one had excellent branding.

panels.scene: The damp route ends at a puddle reflecting a huge cinema entrance. The real entrance in the reflection is behind them.
panels.caption: Route two was mostly reflection.

panels.scene: Under the awning, Scout builds a score table. Both inconvenient routes get ten for MYSTERY. The convenient route gets a question mark.
panels.caption: The criteria needed an editor.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: Do we want mystery or a lens?

panels.scene: Keeper opens a small archive envelope. Inside is a key with a paper tag reading FRONT DOOR. Scout stares at it.
panels.caption: The evidence was unusually clear.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: The key came with the building.

panels.scene: Scout crosses out MYSTERY and adds GETS US INSIDE to the table. The convenient route now has the only checkmark.
panels.caption: A better question made a shorter map.

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: I may have been optimizing the wrong adventure.

panels.scene: They walk the single step to the front door. Scout ceremoniously announces the route with one tiny arrow drawn on a card.
panels.caption: The final plan fit on a thumbnail.

panels.scene: The door swings open. The projector lens sits on a shelf immediately inside, wearing a dust cover shaped like a little cap.
panels.caption: The treasure was expecting them.

panels.scene: Scout places the lens on the projector. Keeper holds the route map up to the light; the puddle stain forms a pleasing oval.
panels.caption: The failed route made a good souvenir.

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: Yes. It has the way back.

panels.scene: They hang the tiny arrow beside the entrance. The grand threaded route map is folded into a simple doormat pattern behind the glass.
panels.caption: The best route was one they could share.

panels.scene: Scout lays a 2 DIRECTIONS art note beside the key. Its reverse reads PLACE. Through the open door, two chairs wait.
panels.caption: A place beats a perfect possibility.

backPage.title: Meet Scout
backPage.shortBio: Can find three fascinating options before breakfast. Practicing the art of choosing one.
fieldGuide: Favorite tool: a map with room to be wrong.
Comic weakness: comparing the route to the route comparison.
New skill: returning.
backPage.bonusObject: A pocket route card with three fields: WHERE / WHY / FIRST STEP.
backPage.readerPrompt: Choose one small place worth returning to. Draw the shortest way there.
backPage.nextIssue: #03 The Missing Credit — Keeper follows a trail of ordinary kindness.

issues.title: The Missing Credit
issues.logline: Keeper investigates an unsigned photograph and finds a kind of care no credit can contain.

cover.title: The Missing Credit
cover.logline: Keeper investigates an unsigned photograph and finds a kind of care no credit can contain.
cover.scene: Keeper stands under a projector beam like a noir streetlamp. Harbor holds an empty picture frame; a tiny lightbulb casts a detective-sized shadow.

note.title: The Unnamed Helper
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: Rain stripes the cinema window. Keeper studies a photograph of the empty auditorium, labeled THE NIGHT THE LIGHT STAYED ON.
panels.caption: Night three. One photograph. No credit.

panels.scene: Harbor holds a magnifying glass over the photograph. It enlarges a single chair leg and nothing useful.
panels.caption: The equipment was committed.

panels.scene: Keeper opens an archive drawer labeled KNOWN. It is full. Another labeled NOT SURE YET is even fuller.
panels.caption: Uncertainty had its own department.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: I cannot file it without a name.

panels.scene: In the photograph, a paper shade hangs crookedly over one lightbulb. Harbor points to the identical shade in the actual lobby.
panels.caption: A crooked clue.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: Our witness has been hanging around.

panels.scene: Beneath the lamp is an old bulb box. Keeper opens it with theatrical care while Harbor steadies the shade.
panels.caption: The case turned on a small box.

panels.scene: Inside the box is a spare bulb and a handwritten slip: FOR THE NEXT PERSON. No signature. Keeper’s magnifier hangs uselessly at their side.
panels.caption: The clue declined to identify itself.

panels.scene: Keeper arranges the photo, box and slip like evidence. A long blank line remains under CREDIT.
panels.caption: The story was bigger than the blank.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: Someone wanted the next person to see.

panels.scene: Keeper writes CREDIT UNKNOWN on the photo sleeve, then adds LIGHT KEPT ON. Harbor nods.
panels.caption: An honest label can hold a mystery.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: I can preserve what we know.

dialogue.speaker: harbor
dialogue.text: And leave room for what we do not.

panels.scene: They replace the old crooked paper shade with a repaired one. The repaired seam remains visible and attractive.
panels.caption: Their addition was a visible seam.

panels.scene: Keeper puts the spare bulb back in the box with the original note and one new slip: THANK YOU, WHOEVER YOU WERE.
panels.caption: The reply did not need an address.

panels.scene: The archive drawer is rearranged. One empty sleeve sits at the front with TODAY written on its tab. Harbor slides the photograph behind it.
panels.caption: The present got a little shelf space.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: Not everything worth keeping has happened.

panels.scene: Under the repaired lamp, a 3 THANK-YOUS art note shows the spare bulb. Its reverse reads TO. The light forms a warm pool over the open sleeve.
panels.caption: Some credits are a light left on.

backPage.title: Meet Keeper
backPage.shortBio: An archivist with the instincts of a detective and an unexpectedly crowded drawer.
fieldGuide: Favorite label: NOT SURE YET.
Secret skill: noticing the contribution outside the frame.
New skill: keeping uncertainty honestly.
backPage.bonusObject: A two-sided object label: WHAT WE KNOW / WHAT WE ARE STILL LEARNING.
backPage.readerPrompt: Write one sentence about an everyday object somebody else cared for.
backPage.nextIssue: #04 A Very Small Countdown — Tempo encounters a kettle with no ambition.

issues.title: A Very Small Countdown
issues.logline: Tempo gives opening-night tea a launch schedule; the kettle refuses a dramatic arc.

cover.title: A Very Small Countdown
cover.logline: Tempo gives opening-night tea a launch schedule; the kettle refuses a dramatic arc.
cover.tagline: ONE GIANT PAUSE FOR A VERY SMALL ROOM.
cover.scene: Tempo stands at a huge graphic countdown. Muse cradles a tiny kettle as if it were a spacecraft. A paper moon hangs from visible string.

note.title: The Room Has a Rhythm
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: A projector displays T-MINUS 60 across the cinema wall. Tempo wears no costume, only a stopwatch; Muse carries two cups.
panels.caption: Night four. A major launch.

dialogue.speaker: tempo
dialogue.text: Tea will begin exactly on the minute.

panels.scene: Tempo has made a control panel from labeled paper switches: CUPS, CHAIRS, KETTLE. Only KETTLE remains unlit.
panels.caption: Mission control was mostly stationery.

dialogue.speaker: muse
dialogue.text: The quiet system is still quiet.

panels.scene: The countdown reaches 30. The kettle gives one tiny, unimpressive bubble. Muse watches it with exaggerated respect.
panels.caption: The vessel resisted narrative pressure.

dialogue.speaker: tempo
dialogue.text: Perhaps it cannot see the timer.

panels.scene: At 10, Tempo leans toward the kettle, stopwatch in front. Muse calmly slides the stopwatch away from the steam.
panels.caption: A tense moment for scheduling.

dialogue.speaker: muse
dialogue.text: We are next to a kettle.

panels.scene: The projected countdown reaches zero. Nothing happens. A paper star on the wall falls down with a tiny TAP.
panels.caption: Liftoff was rescheduled by physics.

panels.scene: Tempo sinks into a chair. Muse catches the paper star and taps it twice against a cup. TAP TAP appears as small type.
panels.caption: Without the clock, another sound arrived.

panels.scene: The room supplies four small sounds: rain at the window, cup on saucer, projector tick and a chair creak. Tempo marks four simple bars.
panels.caption: Rain. Cup. Tick. Creak.

panels.scene: Tempo taps a slow original rhythm on the clipboard. Muse adds one cup tap. The projected zero becomes a large round moon.
panels.caption: They followed the room instead.

dialogue.speaker: tempo
dialogue.text: One. Two. Leave a little space.

panels.scene: The kettle finally clicks. Both stop and look toward it. A tiny burst of steam crosses the paper moon.
panels.caption: The smallest spacecraft arrived.

panels.scene: They sit with tea. Tempo turns the stopwatch face down. Muse places the fallen paper star beside the cups.
panels.caption: No record was set.

dialogue.speaker: muse
dialogue.text: Until we want to get up.

panels.scene: Tempo replaces the giant countdown with a simple card: TEA WHEN READY. Four beat marks form a border.
panels.caption: A schedule with room inside it.

dialogue.speaker: tempo
dialogue.text: I have allocated an unallocated minute.

panels.scene: A 4 BEATS art note lies beneath a cup, safely outside the wet ring. Its reverse reads BE. The stopwatch is still face down.
panels.caption: The souvenir kept the pause.

backPage.title: Meet Tempo
backPage.shortBio: A rhythm specialist learning to hear what happens between the beats.
fieldGuide: Favorite sound: four things almost in time.
Comic weakness: putting a deadline on a good pause.
New skill: listening before counting.
backPage.bonusObject: A four-beat listening card with one deliberately empty beat.
backPage.readerPrompt: Listen for four ordinary sounds. Let one happen without naming it.
backPage.nextIssue: #05 The Poster for Everything — Muse discovers that an invitation needs space.

issues.title: The Poster for Everything
issues.genre: Event-poster spectacle meets economical print wit
issues.logline: Muse designs a poster so epic that nobody can find the event on it.

cover.title: The Poster for Everything
cover.logline: Muse designs a poster so epic that nobody can find the event on it.
cover.tagline: A BIG IDEA NEEDS SOMEWHERE TO SIT.
cover.scene: A monumental poster looms over tiny Muse and Treasury. Its giant starburst is interrupted by one small empty chair and a clear door.

note.title: One Good Invitation
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: Muse unfurls a poster that stretches from the ceiling to the floor. It reads TONIGHT: EVERYTHING in enormous type. Treasury peers around its edge.
panels.caption: Night five. A modest announcement.

panels.scene: Close on the poster: a tiny cinema, a paper moon, seven arrows, a giant cup and a ribbon reading AN UNPRECEDENTED EVENING.
panels.caption: The small print needed its own poster.

panels.scene: Treasury follows an arrow across the poster. The arrow curves around and points back to Treasury’s starting position.
panels.caption: The campaign had excellent retention.

panels.scene: Muse brings out three alternate posters, each larger than the first. One consists entirely of the word SOON.
panels.caption: Four final directions.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: It currently lacks a date and a door.

panels.scene: A breeze lifts the giant poster. Beneath it is an ordinary empty chair with a patch on the seat. Both look at the chair.
panels.caption: Then the furniture interrupted.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: What would make you come here?

panels.scene: Muse sits in the patched chair. The enormous posters curl around them like an unnecessarily elaborate curtain.
panels.caption: A very small answer.

dialogue.speaker: muse
dialogue.text: Somewhere I do not have to impress anyone.

panels.scene: Muse draws one small chair in the center of a clean sheet. Treasury places a single warm-colored swatch beside it.
panels.caption: The idea got smaller. The space got bigger.

panels.scene: The finished poster reads THERE IS ROOM FOR YOU above the small chair. Below: THE BETWEEN / MIDNIGHT / FRONT DOOR.
panels.caption: An invitation finally arrived.

panels.scene: They paste the clean poster into the middle of the old enormous starburst. The result makes the tiny chair look gloriously important.
panels.caption: The spectacle could stay. It had a job now.

panels.scene: Treasury adjusts the poster one millimeter. Muse gently takes the ruler away and leaves the hand-pasted edge visible.
panels.caption: The invitation was allowed to look made.

dialogue.speaker: muse
dialogue.text: It is straight enough to welcome someone.

panels.scene: Muse rolls the rejected posters into a low paper pedestal for the patched chair. Treasury tests it with a careful hand.
panels.caption: Even the extra ideas got a seat.

panels.scene: A 5 POSSIBILITIES art note rests on the chair. Its reverse reads MORE. Behind it, the clean invitation sits inside the enormous starburst.
panels.caption: The final direction had somewhere to go.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: I will record this historic event.

backPage.title: Meet Muse
backPage.shortBio: An art director with five final ideas and one unexpectedly powerful empty chair.
fieldGuide: Favorite phrase: WHAT IF.
Comic weakness: a concept so big the audience needs a map.
New skill: making a clear invitation.
backPage.bonusObject: A two-poster diptych: one tiny object in generous space; the same object at impossible scale.
backPage.readerPrompt: Make a one-object invitation. Give it one headline and one place to go.
backPage.nextIssue: #06 Insert Patience — Sprout challenges the arcade’s definition of progress.

issues.title: Insert Patience
issues.genre: An arcade where the high score needs a rethink
issues.logline: Sprout turns a broken garden arcade into a place where trying is enough to take a turn.

cover.title: Insert Patience
cover.logline: Sprout turns a broken garden arcade into a place where trying is enough to take a turn.
cover.scene: Sprout faces an oversized arcade cabinet with a single tiny sprout in its screen. Scout holds a watering can. A glowing instruction reads INSERT PATIENCE.

note.title: A Turn Is a Beginning
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: In the courtyard, Sprout discovers an old arcade cabinet painted with vines. Its screen is a glass window onto one small seed tray.
panels.caption: Night six. The courtyard had a game.

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: The joystick is a watering can.

panels.scene: A faded scorecard on the cabinet reads MOST VISITS IN A ROW. Sprout places six hopeful stickers beside the single visible seed.
panels.caption: The rules favored enthusiasm.

dialogue.speaker: sprout
dialogue.text: I can do six visits tonight.

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: That may be one very long visit.

panels.scene: Sprout sprinkles a little water, then peers through the glass with a magnifier. The seed looks unchanged.
panels.caption: Progress did not perform for the lens.

panels.scene: Sprout tries the cabinet’s START button. It releases a paper ticket reading COME BACK TOMORROW. A second press releases the same ticket.
panels.caption: A surprisingly consistent reward.

panels.scene: Scout reads the brittle old scorecard. A missing visit is crossed out in red. Sprout imagines a giant zero looming above the tiny seed tray.
panels.caption: The streak made a threat of tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: sprout
dialogue.text: What if someone cannot come back?

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: Then the plant still deserves water.

panels.scene: Sprout puts the stickers down and looks at the courtyard’s dry, empty planters. Scout follows the glance.
panels.caption: The better game was outside the cabinet.

dialogue.speaker: sprout
dialogue.text: Can trying count as a turn?

panels.scene: They remove the scorecard and replace it with three simple choices: LOOK / WATER IF NEEDED / LEAVE A KIND NOTE.
panels.caption: New rules. No losing streak.

panels.scene: Sprout places seed envelopes in the cabinet’s empty ticket compartment. Scout labels a shelf TAKE A QUESTION / LEAVE AN OBSERVATION.
panels.caption: The prize compartment became a beginning.

panels.scene: Scout writes SOIL STILL DAMP on a small card. Sprout puts the watering can down instead of watering again.
panels.caption: Sometimes a good move is not another move.

dialogue.speaker: sprout
dialogue.text: My best turn was leaving it alone.

panels.scene: They sit beside the planter. The arcade window still shows the same small seed. A new sign reads COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN.
panels.caption: Nothing sprouted on cue.

dialogue.speaker: scout
dialogue.text: Should we wait for a big reveal?

panels.scene: Sprout moves the six unused stickers to the cabinet’s edge, making a cheerful border instead of a score. Scout adds a small arrow to the garden.
panels.caption: The stickers found less stressful work.

panels.scene: A 6 TRIES art note rests beside the seed envelope. Its reverse reads THAN. The last frame holds on the seed tray with no forced transformation.
panels.caption: Growth could happen after the panel ended.

backPage.title: Meet Sprout
backPage.shortBio: A patient learner with an impatient sticker collection. Making room for progress that is hard to count.
fieldGuide: Favorite question: CAN TRYING COUNT?
Comic weakness: asking a seed for a progress report.
New skill: taking care without keeping score.
backPage.bonusObject: A garden-arcade card with three optional turns: NOTICE / CARE / SHARE.
backPage.readerPrompt: Try something small. Record one observation without grading yourself.
backPage.nextIssue: #07 Welcome, Eventually — Beacon’s greeting becomes the whole event.

issues.title: Welcome, Eventually
issues.logline: Beacon rehearses an opening welcome so carefully that the first guest never gets inside.

cover.title: Welcome, Eventually
cover.logline: Beacon rehearses an opening welcome so carefully that the first guest never gets inside.
cover.tagline: YOU CAN ARRIVE AS YOU ARE. EVENTUALLY.
cover.scene: Beacon sits behind a tiny late-night desk beneath a huge WELCOME sign. Tempo waits behind a winding velvet rope that loops back to the desk.

note.title: One Clear Hello
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: Beacon has built a welcome desk in the cinema lobby. Seven small signs direct arrivals toward seven other signs. Tempo enters holding a coat.
panels.caption: Night seven. The welcome rehearsal.

panels.scene: Beacon presents a card reading FIRST, YOUR ARRIVAL PREFERENCE. Tempo reaches toward an empty chair just behind the desk.
panels.caption: A personalized beginning.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: Wonderful. That is on page two.

panels.scene: Beacon stands beneath a spotlight and begins a monologue. Tempo remains at the rope, coat still in hand.
panels.caption: The opening had an opening.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: Tonight, we gather to begin the act of gathering—

panels.scene: Beacon points toward a coat-hook sign that points toward a form. Tempo places the coat over one arm and checks the stopwatch.
panels.caption: The hook had prerequisites.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: I wanted nobody to feel unprepared.

panels.scene: A small cue lamp flashes APPLAUSE. Tempo gently taps the coat’s sleeves together. Beacon pauses, hearing how lonely it sounds.
panels.caption: The audience participated responsibly.

panels.scene: The cue lamp goes dark. Beacon notices Tempo is still standing outside the rope. All the signs suddenly look very large.
panels.caption: One fact survived the rehearsal.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: I have not actually let you in.

panels.scene: Beacon lifts the rope, takes the coat and points to the nearest chair. No forms or lights intervene.
panels.caption: A revised program.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: You are welcome here. Want to sit?

dialogue.speaker: tempo
dialogue.text: Yes. That is the whole review.

panels.scene: Both sit on the guest side of the desk. The host chair behind it is empty. Beacon lays the abandoned monologue face down.
panels.caption: The host joined the room.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: What would help you feel at home?

panels.scene: Tempo turns the stopwatch off. Beacon writes TAKE YOUR TIME on the back of the WELCOME sign.
panels.caption: A useful sign with a useful reverse.

panels.scene: They turn six unnecessary directional signs into a playful paper border around the actual entrance. The way in is now obvious.
panels.caption: The directions became scenery.

dialogue.speaker: tempo
dialogue.text: I know exactly where to go.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: I will try not to introduce the doorway.

panels.scene: Beacon tests the new welcome by stepping outside and coming back in. Tempo holds up the two-sided sign without speaking.
panels.caption: A rehearsal with room for silence.

panels.scene: A 7 WELCOMES art note sits on the now-uncluttered desk, reverse WHAT visible. Beside it is one handwritten line: COME AS YOU ARE.
panels.caption: The first guest finally arrived.

backPage.title: Meet Beacon
backPage.shortBio: A host who wants everyone to feel expected. Learning that a welcome can be shorter than a queue.
fieldGuide: Favorite prop: a readable sign.
Comic weakness: an introduction to the introduction.
New skill: asking what would help.
backPage.bonusObject: A reversible door card: WELCOME / TAKE YOUR TIME.
backPage.readerPrompt: Write a welcome in one sentence. Make the next step easy to find.
backPage.nextIssue: #08 The Quiet Side — Harbor asks for a different kind of listening room.

issues.title: The Quiet Side
issues.logline: Harbor leaves a dedication unfinished and discovers that an open space can be a complete gesture.

cover.title: The Quiet Side
cover.logline: Harbor leaves a dedication unfinished and discovers that an open space can be a complete gesture.
cover.tagline: SOME THINGS NEED A QUIET SIDE.
cover.scene: Harbor and Keeper sit beside an unused turntable. An open record sleeve becomes a quiet horizon; a dedication card has one beautiful blank line.

note.title: A Place for the Unsaid
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: At the record stall next to the cinema, Harbor holds an empty sleeve titled ROOM TONE. Keeper carries a pencil and a dedication card.
panels.caption: Night eight. A listening session.

panels.scene: Harbor writes FOR SOMEONE WHO CANNOT BE HERE on the card. The next line remains blank. Keeper offers the pencil again.
panels.caption: The dedication reached a quiet part.

panels.scene: Keeper arranges several possible captions on small slips. They occupy nearly the entire table around Harbor’s single unfinished card.
panels.caption: Kind intentions filled the table.

panels.scene: A tiny desk fan turns the blank record sleeve slightly. Keeper tries to hold down the slips; Harbor watches the moving patch of light.
panels.caption: The room supplied its own track.

panels.scene: Close on three ordinary sounds rendered as small marks: fan, rain gutter, a chair settling. The turntable remains switched off.
panels.caption: No song. Still a sound.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: The chair has a second career.

panels.scene: Harbor quietly slides the extra caption slips aside, making one clear space beside the empty sleeve.
panels.caption: This time Harbor asked.

dialogue.speaker: harbor
dialogue.text: Could we leave this part blank?

panels.scene: Keeper closes the pencil case. The two sit in the cleared space with the dedication card between them.
panels.caption: Nothing rushed in to explain the pause.

panels.scene: Harbor adds one small line at the bottom of the card: A SEAT IS HERE. Keeper moves an empty chair into view beside them.
panels.caption: A few words found their own size.

panels.scene: Keeper holds an archive label above the card but stops. Harbor smiles at the unused label.
panels.caption: The filing system showed restraint.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: Do you want to name the feeling?

dialogue.speaker: harbor
dialogue.text: I would rather keep the evening.

panels.scene: They carry the chair into the cinema and put it near the quiet edge of the room, with a clear path to the door.
panels.caption: The quiet side joined the whole room.

dialogue.speaker: harbor
dialogue.text: I want to sit here sometimes.

dialogue.speaker: keeper
dialogue.text: Then this is also your seat.

panels.scene: Harbor places the card on the chair, then sits beside it rather than retreating out of frame. Keeper sets the empty sleeve on a nearby shelf.
panels.caption: Making room included Harbor.

dialogue.speaker: harbor
dialogue.text: I can be quiet and still be here.

panels.scene: An 8 PAUSES art note rests in the open sleeve. Its reverse reads YOU. The blank line on the dedication card remains visible.
panels.caption: The blank was part of the edition.

dialogue.speaker: harbor
dialogue.text: No need to fill the whole side.

backPage.title: Meet Harbor
backPage.shortBio: Makes room for everyone else. Practicing the small courage of asking for a seat.
fieldGuide: Favorite material: a card with space left over.
Comic weakness: being so considerate nobody hears the request.
New skill: letting a personal need be visible.
backPage.bonusObject: An open dedication card: FOR / A SEAT IS HERE / optional blank space.
backPage.readerPrompt: Write as much or as little as you want for someone or something that matters. Leaving it blank is allowed.
backPage.nextIssue: #09 Please Pass the Moon — Relay learns what a handoff is meant to carry.

issues.title: Please Pass the Moon
issues.genre: Backstage farce with an overqualified handoff
issues.logline: Relay writes instructions so complete that the paper moon never reaches the stage.

cover.title: Please Pass the Moon
cover.logline: Relay writes instructions so complete that the paper moon never reaches the stage.
cover.tagline: THE CONTEXT HAS BECOME THE CARGO.
cover.scene: Relay holds an enormous handoff envelope. Beacon reaches for a small paper moon buried beneath ribbons, labels and a flowchart. The actual screen waits behind them.

note.title: Trust Travels Light
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: In the projection booth, Relay holds a paper moon and a handoff envelope three times its size. Beacon waits below the screen.
panels.caption: Night nine. One last stage task.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: The moon needs to go above the screen.

panels.scene: Relay unfolds a long instruction sheet covering the steps, the reason for the steps and the reason for the reason. The moon is barely visible.
panels.caption: Full context. Possibly more.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: First, the history of the moon.

panels.scene: Beacon takes the envelope. Relay keeps hold of the ribbon attached to it. Both stand still at opposite ends of a small taut line.
panels.caption: A handoff with an attachment.

panels.scene: They pass the envelope back to add one missing note. The paper moon stays on the table through the entire exchange.
panels.caption: The paperwork made the journey.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: We have moved the instructions twice.

panels.scene: The envelope grows a second labeled sleeve: CONTEXT FOR CONTEXT. It now blocks the booth doorway. Beacon looks around it.
panels.caption: The package became the obstacle.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: The moon is lighter than the explanation.

panels.scene: Relay looks from the blocked doorway to the small paper moon still lying untouched on the desk.
panels.caption: A rare alignment of evidence.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: I have handed over everything except the task.

panels.scene: Relay takes a postcard and writes three lines: BEACON / MOON ABOVE SCREEN / BEFORE DOORS OPEN.
panels.caption: One owner. One outcome. One time.

panels.scene: Relay gives Beacon the actual moon and the small postcard, releasing both hands fully. The long ribbon falls harmlessly onto the table.
panels.caption: This time the handoff let go.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: You can choose how to hang it.

panels.scene: Beacon uses a simple clip already above the screen. Relay watches from the booth without offering another diagram.
panels.caption: The solution was someone else’s.

dialogue.speaker: beacon
dialogue.text: It was already a moon-sized clip.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: I had not reached the clip appendix.

panels.scene: The paper moon hangs slightly off center, exactly where it catches the warm projection light. Beacon raises a small DONE card.
panels.caption: Done looked a little different. It worked.

dialogue.speaker: relay
dialogue.text: That is better than my drawing.

panels.scene: They cut the enormous blank back of the instruction sheet into programs for opening night. The old ribbon becomes a neat bow around them.
panels.caption: The context found a smaller audience.

panels.scene: A 9 HANDOFFS art note shows the paper moon and simple clip. Its reverse reads DO. Both stand beneath the finished moon, hands empty.
panels.caption: Trust was the part they could not package.

backPage.title: Meet Relay
backPage.shortBio: Knows how work moves between people. Learning when to stop holding the ribbon.
fieldGuide: Favorite tool: a clear next step.
Comic weakness: a briefing that needs its own briefing.
New skill: accepting a good solution someone else chose.
backPage.bonusObject: A three-line handoff card: WHO / WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE / WHEN.
backPage.readerPrompt: Make one useful handoff brief. Include the context needed to act, then let the recipient choose a method.
backPage.nextIssue: #10 Open for What? — Treasury prepares the last note and opens the real door.

issues.title: Open for What?
issues.genre: An awards-night-sized opening for a very small room
issues.logline: Treasury tries to make opening night feel official, then finds a better reason to print.

cover.title: Open for What?
cover.logline: Treasury tries to make opening night feel official, then finds a better reason to print.
cover.tagline: THE MOST VALUABLE THING IS BEING HERE.
cover.scene: Treasury and Desk Buddy stand at a tiny cinema entrance beneath a monumental paper marquee. Ten art notes form a glowing path to one spare chair.

note.title: The Open Edition
note.label: COLLECTIBLE ART • NO CASH VALUE • NO REDEMPTION

panels.scene: At the box office, Treasury displays a beautifully printed note with a giant 10 and an empty center. Desk Buddy carries the patched chair.
panels.caption: Night ten. The opening edition.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: The chair already thinks it is.

panels.scene: Treasury arranges ribbons, seals and a tiny embossed border around the note. The blank center becomes harder to see.
panels.caption: Authority arrived in layers.

panels.scene: On the wall, the previous nine art-note reverses form A PLACE TO BE MORE THAN WHAT YOU DO. The final rectangle is empty.
panels.caption: Nine nights had left a sentence waiting.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: I still do not have the last word.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: Maybe it is not an award.

panels.scene: Treasury glances at the blank center of the final note, then at the entrance. Desk Buddy’s old clipboard has COME BACK still unchecked.
panels.caption: Nobody had finished belonging.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: Does this note get someone inside?

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: The door does. Admission is free.

panels.scene: Treasury removes the extra seals. On the note’s reverse, they set the word NEXT in plain, confident type.
panels.caption: The last word made room after itself.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: More than what you do next.

panels.scene: The complete ten-note wall reads A PLACE TO BE MORE THAN WHAT YOU DO NEXT. The original OPEN FOR WHAT? brass plate hangs below.
panels.caption: The answer was something they had made.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: We could have printed that on night one.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: We would not have known what it meant.

panels.scene: Treasury pulls the final note from the small press. One corner has a slight ink smudge. Desk Buddy points to the clear text and honest edge.
panels.caption: The first proof had been present for the work.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: So is the chair. Keep going.

panels.scene: Treasury places the notes on a table marked TAKE A SOUVENIR IF YOU LIKE. A separate, larger sign at the entrance reads FREE / COME IN.
panels.caption: The note recorded the night. It did not buy it.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: Good. I came for the company.

panels.scene: Desk Buddy hangs the finished invitation at the open door. Treasury turns the marquee from OPEN FOR WHAT? to OPEN FOR EACH OTHER.
panels.caption: At midnight, the ten gathered.

panels.scene: Focus on Treasury and Desk Buddy seated at the edge of the auditorium. The paper cup and clipboard create a shadow cinema on the screen; other occupied seats remain outside the tight frame.
panels.caption: The first program was wonderfully small.

dialogue.speaker: treasury
dialogue.text: Excellent production values on that cup.

panels.scene: After the show, Treasury sets one extra chair beside the doorway. Desk Buddy places the old clipboard on its seat, COME BACK still open.
panels.caption: One extra seat. One open box.

panels.scene: The final art note lies in the empty chair: 10 PLACES on the front, NEXT visible on a folded reverse sample. Through the doorway, dawn meets the warm cinema light.
panels.caption: End of the first ten nights. Beginning of the place.

dialogue.speaker: desk-buddy
dialogue.text: Put it on the list. Leave the box open.

backPage.title: Meet Treasury
backPage.shortBio: Makes money-shaped souvenirs for things that cannot be bought. Learning to honor a moment without making it official.
fieldGuide: Favorite detail: the honest edge of a printed object.
Comic weakness: another seal will surely explain the feeling.
New skill: recording significance without assigning a price.
backPage.bonusObject: The ten-note wall sentence: A / PLACE / TO / BE / MORE / THAN / WHAT / YOU / DO / NEXT.
backPage.readerPrompt: Make a souvenir of a small moment. Say what it remembers, not what it is worth.
backPage.endCard: 10 PLACES · Reverse fragment 10/10: NEXT · COLLECTIBLE ART. NO CASH VALUE.
backPage.nextIssue: The Between stays open. Somewhere above it, a rooftop radio has begun broadcasting room tone.
